beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A dilation resizes a figure from a fixed center, keeping its shape.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Our center is *O*, the origin at zero, zero. It stays fixed on this side.

do.text: The center need not be the middle

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each point follows a ray that starts at the center and continues straight through the point.

do.text: A straight path from the center

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The scale factor, *k*, is a positive number multiplying each distance from the center.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: With a factor of two, this distance of two units becomes four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: We call the result the image and name its points with prime marks.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The coordinates of *C* mean two left and three up from the origin.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Multiply negative two by two to move four left.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Multiply three by two to move six up, reaching negative four, six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Both coordinates measure from *O*, so both multiply. The arrow means goes to, and *k* *x* means *k* times *x*.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Adding two is a common slip: that puts *C* at zero, five, off its ray; multiply both coordinates to reach negative four, six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A side matches its image side. Here, four becomes eight.

do.text: Matching: a side and its image

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The other sides double too, from three to six and five to ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: As the sides grow, their directions stay unchanged, so the corners never open or close.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The right angle stays ninety degrees, and the other openings stay unchanged too.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: These figures are similar because their shape stays the same.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Congruent figures also have the same size, so our doubled triangle is not congruent.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every factor compares with the blue original. Above one, the image grows.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: It shrinks toward the original, passes through one, and continues to one half.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Both coordinates halve, putting *C* prime at negative one, three halves.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Above one, it grows again. Back at one, every point returns, making the figures congruent too.

do.text: Every factor compares with the original

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Choose *S*, at one, one, as the center where the rays start.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: From *S*, *C* is three left and two up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Double those distances to six left and four up, reaching negative five, five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Multiply coordinates directly only when the chosen center is the origin.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now three more, fast. Center: negative five, negative four. Factor three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Far from the center moves far.

do.text: Far from the center moves far

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Center: five, negative three. Factor one half.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Half the distance on every ray.

do.text: Half the distance on every ray

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Center: negative four, four, on this corner. Factor two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The center never moves; the figure grows away from it.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Any point *P* and its image, *P* prime, share a ray; the distance multiplies by *k*.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: At the origin, multiply both coordinates.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A factor of two enlarges; one half shrinks; one leaves the figure unchanged.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The lengths scale by *k* while the angles stay unchanged.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: From the center, multiply every distance by the same factor. The shape stays the same.
